places.name: Huelva
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit runs wide of the old; 35 houses were built into what was left of it.
The Carmelites were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 26 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit runs wide of the old; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the eastern side; 0 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.
A great fire burned 27 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Vado de Mora
past: The bishop's cathedral and its burg stood on the dry rise; below, the count founded a merchants' town on the waterfront. For a generation they had two councils, then one.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
5 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled.
A great fire burned 34 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

places.name: Puente Real
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The ford was bridged in stone.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 89% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line; 2 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 11 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The Dominicans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 21 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

places.name: Nuestra Señora de la Cinta
past: Farms and an alehouse about a green where the roads meet; a weekly market was granted in its second age.
4 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
A great fire burned 10 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 30 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
